SCRN.01.note: UC Press's description of Kuleshov's own writings identifies juxtaposition as the source of meanings not contained in either shot alone.

article.title: Kuleshov on Film
article.source: Lev Kuleshov — University of California Press

exercise.prompt: Edit the same neutral face against food, a coffin and a child at play, then ask viewers what emotion or intention they inferred from each sequence.

SCRN.02.note: The critical article examines Campbell's model as an influential storytelling tool while challenging its dominance, cultural selectivity and claim to universality.

article.title: One Myth to Rule Them All and in the Darkness Bind Them: A Critical Examination of Joseph Campbell's The Hero's Journey

exercise.prompt: Map one film onto the Hero's Journey, mark stages that must be stretched or omitted, then outline a different story whose structure resists the template.

SCRN.03.note: BFI's discussion of filmmakers who break classical grammar makes the normal continuity system visible: screen direction, eyelines, matching action and the 180-degree axis.

article.title: 4 Hard-and-Fast Rules of Filmmaking… and How The Passion of Joan of Arc Breaks Them

exercise.prompt: Shoot a short two-person exchange twice: once with consistent axis, eyelines and match-on-action, and once with deliberate violations; compare spatial comprehension.

SCRN.04.note: The ASC manual's scope shows cinematography as an integration of lenses, exposure, lighting, colour science, sensors, composition and production workflow.

exercise.prompt: Shoot one scene with two focal lengths and two lighting ratios while preserving exposure, then compare perspective, depth, facial rendering, contrast and emotional emphasis.

SCRN.05.note: The Academy's sound-and-music guide explains production sound, dialogue replacement, sound effects and Foley through practical classroom activities.

article.title: Sound and Music Activities Guide
article.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

exercise.prompt: Mute a one-minute scene and rebuild footsteps, cloth, props, ambience and designed effects from recorded household objects, synchronising each sound to picture.

SCRN.06.note: Blackmagic's official training separates technical correction from creative grading and teaches scopes, shot matching, primary balance, secondary isolation and look development.

exercise.prompt: Balance three mismatched shots with scopes before creating a look, then make warm-cool and low-high contrast variants while preserving skin and neutral references.

SCRN.07.note: The Academy's Jurassic Park programme documents the landmark blend of animatronics, stop-motion knowledge, practical photography and CGI rather than framing effects as a simple either-or choice.

article.title: Jurassic Park
article.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

exercise.prompt: Break one creature shot into practical, digital and compositing layers and explain how shared lighting, camera motion, contact, shadows, texture and scale sell the integration.

SCRN.08.note: McCloud's own presentation introduces comics as a visual language where sequence, simplification, panel choice and reader inference create time and action between images.

exercise.prompt: Tell the same action in three six-panel pages using different panel transitions and gutter sizes, then compare how much motion and time the reader must infer.

SCRN.09.note: The Open University's film-music resource treats music as structurally related to image, character, mood and narrative, providing a foundation for analysing recurring themes and leitmotifs.

article.title: Using Film Music in the Classroom

exercise.prompt: Compose a short leitmotif for one character and transform its tempo, harmony, orchestration and contour for safety, threat, loss and return.

SCRN.10.note: The storytelling principle is treated as setup and payoff rather than a literal requirement that every object must become plot machinery.

article.title: Chekhov’s Gun — Everything You Need to Know

exercise.prompt: Audit a short story scene by scene, marking setup, reminder, escalation and payoff; remove details that neither deepen character, atmosphere nor causality.

SCRN.11.note: The Library of Congress traces the Production Code from industry self-regulation through stricter enforcement and eventual replacement by ratings, making its creative pressure historically concrete.

article.title: When ‘Pre-’ Met ‘Code’ — Eighty Years Ago Today

exercise.prompt: Take one prohibited subject and write two versions of a scene: explicit and Code-era implied, using framing, dialogue, reaction, ellipsis, metaphor and off-screen space.

SCRN.12.note: BFI's cinematography tour explains how Academy, widescreen and Scope formats arose from technical and commercial systems and then became compositional choices.

exercise.prompt: Frame the same scene in 1.33:1, 1.85:1 and 2.39:1 without cropping afterward, then compare faces, groups, environment, movement and negative space.
